summary: Iteration 10: Tested the new adviser 'award' field end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests pass covering /my-adviser & /adviser/profile exposing the field with correct value for Mark, PUT persistence, empty-award clearing, 120-char boundary accepted, 121+ chars returns 422, and light regression on firm info + assessments. Frontend (390x844): client Tom sees the gold-accent 'adviser-award' card with 'AWARD WINNER' label and text 'Protection Adviser of the Year 2026 · Next Intelligence Awards' positioned between Mark's photo/bio and the 'Let's close the gap' section (layout clean, left gold border, award icon). Adviser Mark sees the pre-filled 'Award (optional)' field on /adviser-settings; edit + save works (settings-saved toast appears). Mark's award was RESTORED to the exact original value and verified via /api/my-adviser.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1089 lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, adviser, firm, leads, assessments) in a future iteration. Not blocking.
adviser_profile() always returns 'award' key (default empty string from User model) so clients with blank award cleanly hide the card via truthiness check in adviser.tsx (verified).
seed_data_creation: None. Modified Mark's award during testing then restored it to 'Protection Adviser of the Year 2026 · Next Intelligence Awards'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mark's award is set to 'Protection Adviser of the Year 2026 · Next Intelligence Awards'. The adviser-award testID is only rendered when award is truthy; the AdviserProfileIn pydantic model enforces max_length=120 so PUT with 121 chars returns 422. Tests use '-o addopts=' to disable xdist parallel execution because the pytest.ini forces -n/--dist and our fixtures were originally module-scoped (now function-scoped so parallel should also work, but running serially is safer when mutating Mark's profile).
